description: In FFmpeg's H.264 decoder, slice_table (h264dec.h) is a uint16_t array memset to 0xFFFF as a 'no slice' sentinel, while slice_num = ++h->current_slice is an uncapped int. At slice 65535, slice_num == 0xFFFF, so comparisons against the never-written spare slice_table entries (one per row, mb_stride = mb_width + 1) spuriously match. This defeats the deblock_topleft check in h264_mb.c:532 and the topleft/top guards in h264_mvpred.h:564, leaving deblock_top and deblock_topleft true at mb_x == 0. xchg_mb_border then computes top_border_m1 = sl->top_borders[top_idx][sl->mb_x - 1] (index -1, 96 bytes below the allocation) and performs AV_SWAP64 at offsets -88, -72, -56 — three 8-byte OOB writes whose values are decoded pixel data (src_y - 7) and thus attacker-controlled via DCT coefficients. Trigger requires disable_deblocking_filter_idc = 2 in the slice header, which the attacker sets.
reproduction: 1. Craft an H.264 picture with ~65536 slices so that ++h->current_slice reaches 0xFFFF.
2. Set disable_deblocking_filter_idc = 2 so the deblock_topleft check consults slice_table instead of mb_x > 0.
3. On the 0xFFFF-th slice, spare slice_table entries (still 0xFFFF) compare equal to slice_num; guards in h264_mb.c:532 and h264_mvpred.h:564 fail open.
4. At mb_x = 0, xchg_mb_border indexes top_borders[top_idx][-1] and executes XCHG/AV_SWAP64 at base-88, base-72, base-56.
5. Choose DCT coefficients so decoded src_y pixels — the values swapped in — are attacker-chosen bytes.
technical_details:
Hi --

I've found another vulnerability with Claude that dates to the

original H.264 decoder commit in 2003. I believe it affects every

release. The PoC is large (~780 KB) because the trigger is a picture

with 65536 slices.

This one fires during frame decode, not just probe, so to reproduce it

you have to process the file

  ffmpeg -i h264_slice_sentinel.h264 -f null -

The bug is a comes up because in h264dec.h, slice_table is a uint16_t

array that records which slice owns each macroblock. It's initialized

via memset(..., -1, ...), and so every entry starts as 0xFFFF, used as

a "no slice here yet" marker. Spare entries (one per row, because

mb_stride = mb_width + 1) never get written by decode and stay 0xFFFF

permanently.

At the same time, slice_num = ++h->current_slice is an uncapped int.

The existing code has a log warning ("Possibly too many slices") but

no hard limit.

At slice 65535, slice_num == 0xFFFF. Now every comparison of the form

slice_table[spare_entry] == slice_num passes. Two guards fail open

because of this:

  // h264_mb.c:532 -- first guard

  if (sl->deblocking_filter == 2) {

      deblock_topleft = h->slice_table[sl->mb_xy - 1 - ...] == sl->slice_num;

  // h264_mvpred.h:564 -- second guard (the != variant)

  if (h->slice_table[topleft_xy] != sl->slice_num) {   // 0xFFFF !=

0xFFFF -> FALSE

      sl->topleft_type = 0;                            // never runs

      if (h->slice_table[top_xy] != sl->slice_num)

          sl->top_type = 0;                            // never runs

  }

  // top_type retains stale nonzero value -> deblock_top = sl->top_type is true

With both guards bypassed, xchg_mb_border runs at mb_x = 0:

  // h264_mb.c:543, 559-562

  top_border_m1 = sl->top_borders[top_idx][sl->mb_x - 1];   // [-1] -> base - 96

  ...

  if (deblock_top) {

      if (deblock_topleft) {

          XCHG(top_border_m1 + (8 << pixel_shift),

               src_y - (7 << pixel_shift), 1);

top_borders is uint8_t (*[2])[96]. Index -1 is 96 bytes below the

allocation; the XCHG target at +8 is 88 bytes below.

XCHG expands to AV_SWAP64 -> {tmp = b; b = a; a = tmp}. ASan fires on

the read (first error wins) but the write follows unconditionally in a

non-instrumented build. The non-chroma444 path does two more swaps at

-72 and -56 -- three writes total, 24 bytes. The values written are

decoded pixel data (src_y - 7), so attacker-controlled via DCT

coefficients.

The trigger needs disable_deblocking_filter_idc = 2 in the slice

header (attacker-controlled -- that's what makes it check slice_table

instead of just checking mb_x > 0).

I've against current master (f73849887c):

  ==160422==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow on address

0x51b000008528

  READ of size 8 at 0x51b000008528 thread T0

      #0 xchg_mb_border libavcodec/h264_mb.c:561:13

      #1 hl_decode_mb_simple_8 libavcodec/h264_mb_template.c:155:17

  0x51b000008528 is located 88 bytes before 1460-byte region

  SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow libavcodec/h264_mb.c:561:13

I think the simplest fix is to refuse slice_num >= 0xFFFF.

diff --git a/libavcodec/h264_slice.c b/libavcodec/h264_slice.c

index 69f70c90bb..fb1d947e5b 100644

--- a/libavcodec/h264_slice.c

+++ b/libavcodec/h264_slice.c

@@ -1979,6 +1979,14 @@ static int h264_slice_init(H264Context *h,

H264SliceContext *sl,

                           h->ps.pps->chroma_qp_index_offset[1]) +

                    6 * (h->ps.sps->bit_depth_luma - 8);

+    /* slice_table is uint16_t initialized to 0xFFFF as a sentinel. If

+     * slice_num reaches 0xFFFF, comparisons against spare entries in

+     * slice_table spuriously succeed. */

+    if (h->current_slice >= 0xFFFE) {

+        av_log(h->avctx, AV_LOG_ERROR, "Too many slices (> %d)\n", 0xFFFE);

+        return AVERROR_INVALIDDATA;

+    }

+

     sl->slice_num       = ++h->current_slice;

     if (sl->slice_num)

65534 is still a crazy number of slices so I don't think this rejects

anything real, but you'd know better than me if there's some

pathological-but-legitimate use case that you want to allow. I've

submitted a PR with this for the time being.

Thanks,

Nicholas
title: Heap underflow in H.264 xchg_mb_border via slice_num/sentinel collision
